title: Blanquette de Veau
subtitle: French veal in cream and white sauce with mushrooms
excerpt: Blanquette de veau is a classic of French bourgeois cooking: veal poached in a pale, aromatic broth, then the broth is enriched with cream and egg yolks to produce a silky white sauce. The veal stays white throughout -- it is never browned. The result is one of the gentlest, most elegant stews in the French repertoire.
sourceNotes: Blanquette de veau is one of the benchmark recipes of classical French cooking. The name comes from blanc (white) -- the meat is not browned at any stage, and the finished sauce should be a creamy ivory colour. The dish appears in Escoffier and is a standard of French home cooking. The cream-and-yolk liaison is the classic French technique for thickening and enriching a white sauce without making it heavy.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Can be made up to the stage of adding the cream liaison. Reheat gently and add the cream-yolk mixture at the end.

content.text: The key technique is the cream-and-yolk liaison at the end. This is different from a simple cream sauce: the egg yolks thicken the sauce as well as enrich it. The liaison must be added off the heat, or with the heat very low. If the sauce boils after the liaison goes in, the yolks scramble and the sauce breaks into curds. Mix the yolks and cream together in a bowl first, then temper them by stirring in a ladleful of hot broth before adding back to the pot.
Put {{veal-shoulder}} veal in a large pot and cover with cold water. Bring to a boil. Drain immediately and rinse the veal. This step removes impurities and keeps the sauce white.

Return the veal to the pot with {{chicken-stock}} stock, {{carrots}} carrots, {{celery}} celery, {{shallots}} shallots, {{thyme-fresh}} thyme, {{bay-leaves}} bay leaves, {{black-peppercorns}} peppercorns, and {{salt-table}} salt. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 1 hour until the veal is tender.

Remove the veal with a slotted spoon. Strain and reserve 600 ml of the broth. In a clean pan, melt {{unsalted-butter}} butter over medium heat. Stir in {{plain-flour}} flour and cook for 2 minutes. Gradually whisk in the reserved broth. Simmer for 10 minutes until smooth and thick. Add {{mushrooms-chestnut}} mushrooms and cook for 5 minutes.

Mix {{double-cream}} cream with the {{eggs}} egg yolks and {{lemon}} lemon juice. Remove the pan from the heat. Stir in a ladleful of hot sauce into the yolk mixture, then pour everything back into the pan. Return to very low heat and stir for 2 minutes -- do not let it boil. Add the veal. Serve with rice or boiled potatoes.

items.symptom: The sauce is lumpy or curdled after adding the cream
items.cause: The sauce was too hot when the liaison was added, or it boiled after.
items.fix: If it has curdled but not badly, whisk vigorously off the heat. Pass through a sieve if needed. Next time, temper the yolks by adding hot sauce to them slowly before adding back, and never let the sauce boil after the liaison goes in.

content.text: Blanquette de veau is one of the most loved dishes in French home cooking. It was voted the most popular dish in France in a 1980 survey. The dish is associated with Sunday lunch and with winter, and it has remained unchanged for generations. It is taught in every French cooking school as a classic example of the liaison technique.
